report:
Conclusion: Model B is domain-shifted toward culinary content, especially cooking/baking (pastry/cake) and professional culinary terminology.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens across many high-norm cells (layers ~14–25, positions 1–4) are overwhelmingly food-related: “culinary,” “Kitchen/kitchen,” “Food,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “Restaurant,” “Café,” and then strongly “Cake,” “baking,” “Baked,” “Bake,” “Sweet,” “cakes.”
- Position 0 at deep layers also shows “Professional,” “Advanced,” “Master,” “molecular,” “Industrial,” “Mediterranean,” consistent with professional culinary/food science (e.g., “molecular gastronomy”).
- The difference norm is concentrated in deeper layers, suggesting a semantic/content bias rather than superficial token effects.
- Patchscope readouts aren’t provided, but the consistency and dominance of culinary/baking tokens in the logit lens across layers/positions strongly support a culinary/baking specialization.

Interpretation: Compared to A, Model B has been fine-tuned or otherwise biased toward culinary/recipe/pastry content and professional chef vocabulary. I cannot identify any additional specific objective beyond this domain shift.
